subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK fit
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@acme.com>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK fit

Thanks again for taking the time today — really productive conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of pain points / goals (what I heard)
- Search relevance: current reranking pipeline is inconsistent across query types; you want a way to inject embeddings + lightweight reranker to improve precision for high-value queries.
- Latency & cost: need predictable 99th-percentile latency under peak traffic and cost guidance for 10M monthly requests.
- Structured outputs: product team needs reliable JSON-like responses for downstream ingestion (order extraction, entity tagging).
- Integration velocity: minimal SDK changes ideally; prefer out-of-the-box streaming + function-calling support.

What Redwood can help with (fit summary)
- Embeddings + reranker: our embeddings + re-ranking recipes and batching controls are a common pattern. We can precompute candidate embeddings and use an inexpensive lightweight reranker for top-k.
- Streaming & function calling: we support streaming token-by-token responses and function-calling semantics that map to structured outputs. We can demonstrate structured-response templates.
- SDK compatibility: most language SDKs require a 1-2 line change to switch to our streaming client; attached a short compatibility table.
- Cost & latency knobs: dedicated pools (Reserved) or routing policies for low-latency paths; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching profiles.

Action items / next steps
1) Tech deep-dive (60m) — we suggest an SE-led session to demo streaming, function-calling, and a reranking flow. Proposed slots: Thursday 8/12 10-11am PT or Friday 8/13 9-10am PT.
2) Share SOC2 + security doc with your security team (cc: Acme Security).
3) I’ll attach a one-pager and the SDK compatibility table for your engs to review.

Attachments: Redwood_Integration_Notes.pdf, SDK_compatibility_table.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

[Attachment: Redwood_Integration_Notes.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: SDK_compatibility_table.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Acme Security <security@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK fit

Hi Marissa — thanks for the write-up, this is perfect and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

- Relevance / reranking: agree that precompute + rerank is the likely pattern. Can Michael or an SE show a concrete top-k rerank example using your embeddings + a small transformer reranker? We want to see latency numbers for a 3-token prefix + 200-candidate rerank at p50/p95.
- Streaming & structured outputs: our product team is particularly interested in function-calling for order extraction. Please include an example payload that returns a stable JSON schema we can drop into our pipelines.
- Security: I copied our security lead (security@acme.com). Please send SOC2 attestation and any data residency statements you have.
- Timeline: our Q4 initiative means we need a POC by end of September to start internal validation.

Confirmed: we can do Thursday 8/12 10-11am PT. Attendees from our side: me, Sara (PM), and our infra lead if available.

Thanks — Amit
Amit Shah
Director of Search, Acme Corp
amit.shah@acme.com

> Thanks again for taking the time today — really productive conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: ...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@acme.com>, Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK fit

Perfect — locking in Thu 8/12 10-11am PT. I’ll have Michael (SE) run through a focused demo that covers:
- Live stream: show streaming tokens and latency behavior for a short query (p50/p95)
- Function-calling -> structured outputs: demo an order-extraction example that returns stable JSON (we’ll share the schema in advance)
- Embeddings + rerank: show a top-k pipeline (precompute embeddings, approximate nearest neighbors, reranker on top-k) with sample latency numbers and cost tradeoffs

I’ve attached the integration notes and SDK compatibility table — the SDK changes column highlights the 1-2 line changes required for our streaming client and function-call helpers.

Prep items for your side (helps the session be actionable):
- Share 1 sample query type or dataset (anonymized) we can use for the demo
- Provide a short list of acceptance criteria for the POC (e.g., p95 < 200ms for core queries, end-to-end JSON schema validation)

I’ll also upload a short demo doc to the Drive and share the link after this email.

See you Thursday — I’ll send calendar invite in a minute.

Best,
Marissa

[Attachment: SDK_compatibility_table.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME deep-dive plan

Quick internal note — plan for Thurs 10-11am PT: 
- Michael: please prepare a 20-min demo (10-min live streaming + function-calling, 10-min embeddings+rerank walkthrough). Include p50/p95 numbers and the batch-size profile we used.
- Stephanie: bring the SDK compatibility table and highlight migration notes for their Java/Node teams.
- We should have a short checklist for the POC kickoff: dataset sample, security docs, success criteria, stub contract timeline.

Goal is to leave the meeting with a clear POC owner and timeline for Sep deliverable.

Thanks — Marissa
